title: Joly asks Competition Bureau to investigate Cleveland-Cliffs purchase of Stelco
summary: Canada's industry minister is asking the Competition Bureau to investigate Stelco's parent company after its CEO told CBC News that he only bought the Hamilton steelmaker to stop it undercutting his…

image.caption: Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says she is calling for the investigation after what she called the CEO's 'confessions' about the purchase of Stelco. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Canada's industry minister is asking the Competition Bureau to investigate Stelco's parent company after its CEO told CBC News that he only bought the Hamilton steelmaker to stop it undercutting his U.S. business.
CEO said he bought Hamilton plant to stop it undercutting U.S. company
Mélanie Joly said on Friday she has sent a letter to the competition commissioner asking them to examine whether Cleveland-Cliffs's conduct ran afoul of the Competition Act.
"If negotiations and acquisition were conducted in bad faith, Canadians deserve to know. The company needs to face the consequences," she said in a statement.

Last week, Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves told CBC's Power & Politics with David Cochrane "I bought Stelco because I could not afford anymore having Stelco flooding the market here in the United States to the detriment of my own company."
Stelco owner's live TV admission prompts industry minister to call lawyers
Joly called that a "shocking admission" and said she contacted the department's lawyers to see if there should be any consequences.
"It is the commissioner's responsibility to examine this matter thoroughly and, if warranted, take the appropriate measures," she said on Friday.
Goncalves made his comments after Joly's demand that the company reverse its layoffs at Stelco or face potential legal action.

Stelco owner says he could sell plant next year

blocks.text: The government says the company agreed when it purchased Stelco to keep the number of unionized employees at 2024 levels through to 2029.
Goncalves's company maintains that it's in "full compliance" with the obligations it made under the Investment Canada Act.
